reasoning_traces.think:
The GSE Score Engine operates as a shadow-only decision-quality layer that aggregates five distinct concepts into a scalar GSE Action Score. Modeled probability (P_model) represents the collective model parliament’s belief about an outcome. Confidence score (C) measures internal agreement and evidence health, acting as a reliability proxy. Feature contract (F_contract) enforces data validity, blocking execution if inputs are stale or non-compliant. No-bet strength (S_nobet) introduces a suppression mechanism that biases against action when uncertainty is high. These components combine into a 0–100 GSE Action Score without claiming calibrated win probability. The engine uses guardrails such as HARD_PASS on missing/stale data and blocks calibration claims unless validated. Decision states—PLAY, LEAN, WATCH, PASS—are determined by thresholds on the composite score and no-bet strength. This architecture avoids conflating decision quality with outcome probability, maintaining separation of concerns across model inference, data governance, and action control.
